newsitem.title: UK: London precious metals shed signs of recent rally.
newsitem.headline: London precious metals shed signs of recent rally.

text.p: The precious metals were weaker amid renewed bearish sentiment on Monday, and platinum slumped to fresh three-year lows.
"It's very disappointing that all the markets turned around after a real burst to the upside on Friday, especially gold, which has really given up the ghost," a dealer said.
Bullion fixed at $368.50 an ounce, against $370.25 on Friday afternoon and a London close of $369.40/$369.90.
Gold prices had rallied strongly early on Friday as speculators anticipated a move of "hot" money on comments by U.S. Federal Reserve chairman Alan Greenspan.

But values had rapidly turned lower, coming off highs near $375 an ounce after weaker-than-forecast U.S. jobs data restored some financial market confidence. But the brief price surge could help boost physical demand for gold, dealers said. "Support should now emerge around $367-$368," one noted. Platinum prices were trading at a small discount to gold after fixing below the psychological $370 an ounce support level for the first time in more than three years.
Platinum fixed at $368.00 an ounce, a fresh low since December 1, 1993, after sinking on Friday to fix at $370.25.
"Platinum looks pretty bad, it hasn't been here for a long time," a dealer said.
Platinum was likely to find good support at $365, but its discount to gold could ease to minus $5.
The decline was likely due to investment funds liquidating long platinum positions that had been held in a play on the gold-platinum spread, the dealer said.
But a senior Russian trade official in Tokyo noted that major exporter Russia may be selling some platinum in Europe in a bid to fill export quotas approved for this year.
"Some quantity of platinum is probably being sold in the spot market in Europe because December is the last month to sell from export quota for this year," the official told Reuters.
The price of platinum has been declining steadily for months as imports by leading consumer Japan have been lower this year.

Weekend ethnic clashes near South Africa's Wildebeesfonetein platinum mine, in which at least 37 people were killed, had subsided by late Sunday, police said. Palladium was down $0.75 at $114.75/$115.75 an ounce.
Silver was also weaker, influenced by gold, at $4.75/$4.77, a drop of five cents from Friday. Dealers expected it to trade in a broad $4.70-$5.00 range in coming days.
